headline: Today's faster tempo effort sat at a notably lower HR than a comparable hard run ten days ago.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Today's 6.6 km at low-5s pace came in with heart rate well below where your late-June harder effort landed at a quicker pace — that late-June run cost you a much higher HR and load for its speed. Taken alongside the easy-run HR trend that's been building over the past two weeks, this is another data point pointing the same direction: your aerobic engine is running more efficiently at these paces. One faster session doesn't confirm anything on its own, but it's consistent with the economy picture the easy runs have been painting.

Volume is essentially holding flat versus the prior block, and strength frequency has actually ticked up rather than slipping — a good sign given the recurring concern about strength getting squeezed as running load stays high. Zone 2 minutes have climbed back above the weekly floor, resolving the earlier worry about easy volume getting crowded out. This looks like a consolidating block with the pieces staying in balance rather than any one quality being sacrificed.

With St. Olavsleden about a month out, the demand still least represented in your recent data is loaded back-to-back time on feet — long, consecutive days under a 6-8 kg pack. Your fitness signals are trending well, but that specific durability quality isn't something the current run profile is testing.
watch_items: Whether loaded, consecutive-day efforts appear in the coming weeks — that pack-carrying durability is the gap closest to the event demand.
Whether today's lower HR at faster paces holds up across repeated tempo sessions rather than a single occurrence.
Sleep scores have been erratic and mostly low this week; worth noting if that coincides with any flattening in the HR trend, though the data stream is still too new to act on.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 140 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 7 runs)
▲ 4-week volume 139 km vs 133 km prior block (+5%)
▲ Zone 2: 192 min vs 180-240 min/week target (107% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 1.2%
